name: Thailand
summary: Thai residents (more than 180 days a year) pay progressive tax up to 35% on Thai income and, since 2024, on foreign income earned from 1 January 2024 whenever it is remitted to Thailand (pre-2024 income stays exempt even if remitted). Gains on shares sold on the Stock Exchange of Thailand are exempt; Thai dividends can be taxed at a final 10%. Foreign dividends and gains kept abroad are not taxed. Inheritance tax applies at 5% for children on amounts above THB 100 million received from each deceased; gifts from parents to children above THB 20 million a year are taxed at 5%. Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa holders in the wealthy categories are exempt on remitted foreign income.

regimes.name: Thai tax resident
regimes.description: Progressive 0-35% on Thai-source income and on foreign income earned from 2024 when remitted to Thailand.
regimes.eligibility: Present in Thailand for more than 180 days in the calendar year. Foreigners need a long-stay visa (e.g. LTR, Thailand Privilege/Elite, retirement).

capital_gains.summary: No separate CGT: gains are ordinary income at up to 35%, but gains on SET-listed shares sold through the exchange and on mutual fund units are exempt. Foreign gains are taxed only if remitted to Thailand; under Revenue Department orders Paw. 161/2566 and 162/2566, foreign income earned from 1 January 2024 is taxable when remitted in that or any later year.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: SET-listed shares sold on the exchange: exempt. Thai mutual fund units: exempt. Foreign income earned before 2024: exempt when remitted. Capital losses cannot offset gains.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Gains on Thai real estate sold by individuals are taxed through a special withholding computation on the appraised value with deductions for years held, plus specific business tax if held under 5 years (not verified in detail; local real estate rate left null). Digital-asset gains through licensed Thai exchanges exempt 2025-2029.

sources.title: Thailand - Individual - Taxes on personal income

capital_gains.rate_basis: Foreign shares and foreign real estate: 35% top marginal rate applies only to gains earned from 2024 and remitted to Thailand; 0% if kept abroad. SET shares exempt. Private (unlisted Thai) company sale: ordinary income up to 35%. Local real estate: special regime not verified, left null.
capital_gains.professional_trader: No separate trader test for SET shares (exempt in any case). Foreign trading gains are subject to the same remittance rule.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Taxed on remittance only (income earned from 1 January 2024). Credit for foreign tax only where a tax treaty allows it.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Remittance basis: the 35% rates on foreign shares and foreign real estate ASSUME the gain is remitted to Thailand (Revenue Department orders Paw. 161/2566 and 162/2566: foreign income earned from 1 January 2024 is taxable when brought into Thailand in that or any later year). Gains kept abroad are not taxed (0%). The scoring uses the remitted case.

dividends.summary: Thai dividends bear a 10% withholding tax that residents may treat as final (or include in income and claim a dividend credit). Foreign dividends are taxed at progressive rates up to 35% only if earned from 2024 and remitted to Thailand; credit for foreign tax only under a treaty.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: First THB 150,000 of net income exempt (general band).
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign tax credit is available only under a double tax treaty (61 treaties, including the US).

sources.title: Thailand - Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 10% final WHT election. Foreign: 35% top rate if remitted (0% if kept offshore), with treaty-based credit.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% final WHT on dividends paid to foreign companies not doing business in Thailand (treaty-reducible).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 20%; Thai holding company dividends from Thai companies may be partly or fully exempt (not verified).
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Remittance basis: the 35% foreign_gross_rate ASSUMES the dividends are remitted to Thailand (Paw. 161/2566 and 162/2566). Foreign dividends kept abroad are not taxed (0%). Thai dividends: 10% final withholding regardless.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Land and building tax on property values (rates not verified). Foreigners cannot generally own land; condominium units are allowed within the foreign quota.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance tax (Inheritance Tax Act B.E. 2558, 2015) is levied on the heir: the value above THB 100 million received from each deceased person is taxed at 5% for descendants and ascendants (10% for others); spouses are exempt. Gifts from parents to their legitimate children are exempt up to THB 20 million per child per year; the excess is taxed at 5% as income tax on the recipient.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: THB 100 million per heir per testator; spouse exempt; gifts to children THB 20 million per child per year.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Taxable property includes immovable property, securities, bank deposits, registered vehicles and prescribed financial assets; it covers worldwide property for Thai nationals and Thai-domiciled foreigners, but only Thai property for other foreigners (general rule from the Act, not verified in this session).
inheritance.spouse_note: An inheritance received by the deceased's spouse is outside the Inheritance Tax Act B.E. 2558 whatever its size (Thai law-firm summaries; the statute section was not located). Other heirs pay 5% (descendants, ascendants) or 10% above THB 100 million.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts from parents to legitimate children above THB 20 million per child per year are taxed at 5% (income tax on the donee, not aggregated with other income).
inheritance.foreign_assets: For foreign nationals not domiciled in Thailand, only Thai-situs property is believed to be in scope (not verified).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Heir-based: applies to Thai nationals, and to foreigners domiciled in Thailand (worldwide property) or receiving Thai property (not verified).

regimes.name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa - Wealthy Global Citizen / Wealthy Pensioner
regimes.description: LTR visa holders in these categories are exempt from Thai tax on overseas income remitted to Thailand (BOI list of privileges: 'tax exemption for overseas income'; Royal Decree No. 743, not opened).
regimes.eligibility: Wealthy Global Citizen: at least USD 1 million in assets and USD 500,000 invested in Thai government bonds, Thai companies or Thai property before applying. Wealthy Pensioner: age 50+, passive income of USD 80,000 a year (or USD 40,000-80,000 plus USD 250,000 investment). Spouse and children under 20 (up to 4 dependants). Visa 5 years, renewable for 5.

capital_gains.summary: Foreign gains remitted to Thailand are exempt for LTR holders; Thai gains taxed as standard.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Overseas income (including gains) exempt even if remitted; Thai items as standard.
open_questions: Exact scope of the LTR overseas-income exemption (whether dependants are covered) not verified from the Royal Decree.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: LTR visa holder in the Wealthy Global Citizen or Wealthy Pensioner category: overseas income is exempt even when remitted, so the 0% foreign rates do not depend on keeping money abroad.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends remitted to Thailand are exempt for LTR holders.
dividends.rate_basis: Overseas income exempt; Thai dividends 10% final.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: LTR visa holder in the Wealthy Global Citizen or Wealthy Pensioner category: overseas income is exempt even when remitted, so the 0% foreign rates do not depend on keeping money abroad.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if present in Thailand for more than 180 days in aggregate in a calendar year.

routes.name: Long-Term Resident visa (Wealthy Global Citizen)
routes.requirements: USD 1 million in assets plus USD 500,000 invested in Thailand; dependants included; 5+5 years.

routes.name: Long-Term Resident visa (Wealthy Pensioner)
routes.requirements: Age 50+, USD 80,000 a year of passive income (or USD 40,000+ with a USD 250,000 investment).

corporate.summary: 20% CIT (graduated rates for small companies). Pillar Two: QDMTT, IIR and UTPR from fiscal years beginning 1 January 2025 (Top-up Tax Decree, 26 December 2024). 10% WHT on dividends to foreign companies.
corporate.special_zones: Board of Investment (BOI) incentives and Eastern Economic Corridor (not researched).

sources.title: Thailand - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent of 278 unique 4- and 5-bedroom house listings in Watthana district (Sukhumvit, Thong Lo, Ekkamai, Phrom Phong) on Dot Property, first 25 result pages read 15 October 2026 (first quartile THB 120,000, third quartile THB 250,000). Asking rents; duplicates across agents only partly removed. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

source.title: Houses for rent in Watthana, Bangkok (listing search)

intl_school_annual_fee.description: International School Bangkok (Nichada Thani), High School (Grades 9-12) tuition 2026/27 per annum, plus an annual fee of THB 22,000 and a one-time registration fee of THB 260,000.

cost_of_living.notes: Many ISB families live near the school in Nichada Thani (Nonthaburi), where rents are lower than in Watthana. Purchase prices, health insurance and housekeeper costs not sourced. Foreigners cannot own land; condominium units only within the 49% foreign quota.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain US-taxed; the US-Thailand treaty allows Thai credit for US tax on US-source income. The LTR exemption does not affect US tax.
open_questions: Whether any 2025/2026 change to the remittance rule (e.g. a proposed grace period for income remitted within a set time) has been enacted could not be checked (web search budget exhausted); PwC's August 2026 review mentions none.
Thai real estate sale taxation and land and building tax rates not verified.
Inheritance tax scope for non-domiciled foreigners not verified against the Inheritance Tax Act text.
Cost of living: prime rent is a listing-portal median (asking rents), not transaction data; purchase prices, health insurance and housekeeper wages not sourced.
